haiku-low.q1: It gets 401 Unauthorized at step 1 and ends there. The counter store is never touched, so no rate-limit counter changes.
haiku-low.q2: All of a customer's keys share one budget, so the total is the plan limit: 100 per clock minute for Standard. Enterprise is ENTERPRISE_LIMIT, not yet decided.
haiku-low.q3: 429 Too Many Requests with Retry-After in whole seconds. The request is not forwarded, so the backend never sees it.
haiku-low.q4: No. The rejected request was never counted, so it uses no budget.
haiku-low.q5: Yes. The count is taken before forwarding, so a backend response of any status, including 500, still uses the budget.
haiku-low.q6: Fail open: the request is forwarded with no limit check, ratelimit_store_unavailable is emitted, and no X-RateLimit headers are sent. Up to 50 ms added.
haiku-low.q7: Standard: 100 requests per clock minute. Enterprise: ENTERPRISE_LIMIT, not yet decided. Until it is set, Enterprise requests are counted but never rejected.
haiku-low.q8: In a shared Redis counter store, one key per customer and window: rl:{customerId}:{windowIndex}. Each counter expires 60 seconds after creation, which removes old counts.
haiku-low.q9: The window is one clock minute by Redis server time, so a new window index starts a fresh count. Old counters expire 60 seconds after creation. No other recovery is stated.
haiku-low.q10: The check and increment run as one atomic Lua script in Redis, so two instances cannot both read 99 and both proceed.
haiku-low.q11: It is the milliseconds until the window ends, rounded up to whole seconds, with a minimum of 1. Redis computes it inside the Lua script.
haiku-low.q12: Retry: NOT STATED. The client gets the backend's response with no X-RateLimit headers.

sonnet.q1: It gets 401 Unauthorized and the request ends at step 1. No counter is read or changed; the counter store is never touched.
sonnet.q2: All of a customer's keys share one budget, so in total they can send only the plan limit per window (100 per minute for Standard).
sonnet.q3: A 429 Too Many Requests with a Retry-After header in whole seconds. The request is not forwarded, so the backend never sees it. (Whether 429 carries X-RateLimit headers is undecided.)
sonnet.q4: No. A rejected request is not incremented or counted, so it uses no budget.
sonnet.q5: Yes. The count is taken before forwarding, and a backend error of any status, including 500, still uses the budget.
sonnet.q6: Fail open: the request is forwarded with no limit check, the gateway emits the ratelimit_store_unavailable metric, and no X-RateLimit headers are sent. Each request may add up to 50 ms of latency.
sonnet.q7: Standard is 100 requests per clock minute. Enterprise uses ENTERPRISE_LIMIT, which is not yet decided. Until it is set, Enterprise requests are counted but never rejected.
sonnet.q8: In a shared Redis store, as a counter keyed rl:{customerId}:{windowIndex}. Each counter expires 60 seconds after it is created (expiry set when the counter is first created).
sonnet.q9: It recovers when the next clock-minute window starts (by Redis server time), because a new window index means a new counter. The old counter expires 60 seconds after creation.
sonnet.q10: The check and count run as one atomic Lua script in Redis, so two instances cannot both read 99 and both proceed. Standard customers get exactly 100 counted requests per window.
sonnet.q11: It is the milliseconds until the window ends (returned by Redis), rounded up to whole seconds, with a minimum of 1.
sonnet.q12: NOT STATED whether the gateway retries the store. The request is forwarded once (fail open), and the client gets the backend response with no X-RateLimit headers. The gateway emits ratelimit_store_unavailable internally.
